whys.h2: 从四个顶点到宇宙图景的推导脉络。
whys.intro: 在本框架的设定下，以下十一项自然结构特征皆由同一四点对象导出，彼此环环相扣。排列顺序以论证确定性由高到低为序，而非按结论的奇特程度排列。第 01 与第 04 项仅涉及该有限对象本身的组合与代数性质，无需预先接受整个物理框架即可独立验证；第 02 与第 03 项中的计数部分同样数学闭合，而将其落实为现实物理时空的环节则依赖作者标注的开放接口。
whys.scaleNote: 尺度标尺仅标示每项结论所对应的自然现象尺阶，不代表框架已独立推导出该尺度。标尺左端所标示的长度为元胞自身的基本长度单位，属于预先设定的标度约定，而非计算产物。

rows.q: 这个基本对象为什么恰有四个顶点？
rows.answer: 虚数单位 i 有一条不可动摇的代数性质：平方等于 −1，即连续作用两次等价于反向。该 K₄ 元胞会自然衍生出自身的复结构 i：沿四个顶点构成的闭合回路前进一格，即作为其基本演化步长。回路若含 n 个顶点，则每步旋转角度为 360°/n；若要求“连续两步恰好反向 180°”，则必须满足 2 × 360°/n = 180°，唯一正整数解只有 n = 4。三顶点两步旋转 240°，五顶点两步旋转 144°，均无法精确反向。换言之，元胞恰有四个顶点，正因为 i 的循环阶数为四——连作四次方能复原。颜色数则由同一自举定理的其余条款定出：必须为奇数（偶数会引入无法区分手征的实要素——作者自订之手征准则）、至少为三且严格少于顶点数。若引入第四种颜色使四顶点各具一色，系统将退化为唯一完美配色的平庸态，无法分化出物质代际。奇数、不少于三、少于四，在所有组合中唯有 (3, 4) 满足条件。
rows.rides: 不依赖任何开放接口。适用范围仅限于作者自订的一类对象——图上每个顶点设有一个三态基本开关，且仅存在成对两体相互作用；外加框架唯一公设，即此类元胞存在并拼接成晶格。该前提范畴的合理宽度已被作者专列为公开审阅问题。
rows.check: 《K4 元胞》一章“元胞自举定理”第 (i) 款；审阅问题 A。机器核验侧：四分之一圈演化算符的平方等于 −I，而三阶循环算符经证明无法实现（CellBootstrapFixedPoint）；另一独立模块按谱分析排除了所有 n ≥ 5 的情形，因为此类算符将带有超过一对共轭复特征值（CellBootstrapClockUniqueness）。Lean 核验覆盖上述算术与矩阵条款，零 sorry；而“这些条款在物理上必然适用”属于专著理论论证，不由形式化验证担保。
rows.lead: 恰有四个顶点，正因四分之一圈连续旋转两次恰好反向，在代数上即对应于乘以 −1。

rows.answer: 单个元胞共有 81 种经典基态：四个顶点，各取三种颜色，即 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 81。求解其 81 × 81 阶哈密顿矩阵的能谱，全部状态自然分解为四个简并能层，自高而低分别为 15、45、12、9 维，无一冗余。最低能层（基态）恰为 9 维，排布成整齐的 3 × 3 矩阵结构：三行源于三种内部色态，三列源自四个顶点置换对称群 S₄ 下的三个独立不可约方向（四减一得三）。这三列结构，即为本框架中三代费米子的代数起源。物理学史上拉比初见 μ 子时曾问“这是谁点的菜”；在此模型中，三列结构乃基本算术的必然推论。同一代数分解还同时给出：三列之中必有一列单独分布、另两列成对关联，呈一重二轻的等级格局——但它只确定结构格局，不直接赋予绝对质量值。计数得到“3”是闭合定理；而将这三列结构正式映射为时空中的三代夸克与轻子，则是作者列为开放的具名接口。
rows.rides: 计数“3”本身不依赖任何开放接口。但将这一结构数“3”落实为时空中的三代物质粒子、并将七行匿名表示对号入座至标准模型七类场，则依赖作者列为开放的一组具名映射（E8，共四项）。
rows.check: 《K4 元胞》一章“由 Schur–Weyl 对偶给出的味世代”定理，配以“色与味：切勿作范畴混同”注记；数值计算证书见实验 071（精确对角化结果，按能级从低到高简并度依次为 9、12、45、15）。严格而言，这三列对应于置换群 S₄ 的 [2,1,1] Specht 模——即标准表示 [3,1] 伴随一次符号扭转，维数同为 3。一重二轻的对称性破缺格局出自质量保护引理。开放部分对应勘误 E8 所列的四条具名映射：全局世代扩张、完整正则嵌入、实物理分支保持以及 48 维流符号满射；同时亦受 E10 约束。相关审阅问题见 8 与 10。
rows.lead: 该对象最低能层恰好构成三列结构：数字“3”出自代数计数，而非人为设定；落实到物理粒子则须再跨一步。

rows.answer: 光滑的球面具有三个独立的旋转对称生成元。在球面上任定一点：绕该点法线轴的旋转使其保持不动，其余两种旋转则会移动该点位置，因此该点所能遍历的流形——球面本身——是 3 − 1 = 2 维。将球面类比为本框架的元胞内部对称群（SU(3)，共有 8 个独立连续生成元），而基态恰好只对其中 4 个生成元（U(2) 子群）保持不变，被其余 4 个生成元所移动。基态流形自身因而具有 8 − 4 = 4 个局部独立方向；将这些局部切空间光滑拼接起来，便形成四维连续底面，即四维时空。至此时间维度尚未分化，四个方向完全对称。随后，基态内置的模流（modular flow）演化算符在其有定义的区域从四维中选出一条，将其度规符号反号，由此区分为 3 + 1 维时空（而非 4 + 1 维）。另一路独立论证从反方向支撑这一维度数：物质与反物质之间的微小不对称（夸克混合中的 CP 破坏）在本框架内的数学形式恰好要求至少四个维度方能容纳，低于四维则会恒等为零。需注意：顶点数“4”与时空维数“4”来源于两条彼此独立的推导路径——前者出自离散群的阶数，后者出自连续对称群的陪集减法；将两个“4”统一在同一动力学框架下，是本理论明确陈述的识别设定。
rows.rides: 从八个对称生成元破缺至保留四个生成元（SU(3) → U(2)）的陪集计数属于元胞内部闭合数学定理。但在模流尚未赋予时间符号前，这四个维度完全对称（欧几里得符号差）。如何严格完成由欧氏几何向洛伦兹时空的过渡，以及引力场如何自源头涌现，属于作者列为开放的接口（E7）。
rows.check: 《K4 元胞》一章“四维时空作为拓扑必然性”一节：包含拓扑必然性定理（8 − 4 = 4 陪集计数）与 Berry 形式 CP 阻碍定理（(2,2)-形式在低于四维时恒为零），两项在专著中均标为闭合；而“D = 4 的四重选出”属评注而非严格定理。时间分化步骤见模流 Wick 转动引理与“模时间非第五维”评注，在正则坐标卡上闭合，机器端仅检验给定符号差的传递。在 Lean 形式化库中，陪集维数算术已完成核心证明，但 CP² 复几何本身尚未形式化；就 CP 阻碍而言，机器仅按“Jarlskog 不变量非零 ⇒ 至少四维”的条件蕴含式完成核验，并非全几何独立证明。相关接口为勘误 E7；审阅问题见 2 与 3。
rows.lead: 八种内部对称操作减去保持基态不变的四种，余下四个独立移动方向；框架将其对应为四维时空。

rows.q: 这个对象的其余构造，为何同样不是人为挑选的？
rows.answer: 并非唯独顶点数“4”出自数学推导。在作者划定的对象类别内，元胞的每一项几何与代数特征均由自洽条件唯一锁定：四个顶点、三种颜色、两两相连的完全图、等权重的交换耦合，以及倾向异色的“反铁磁”符号——所有这些条款均未引用任何实验测量数值。以耦合符号为例，我们完全可在纸上反向推演：倘若改用倾向同色的“铁磁”规则，所有顶点只需取同一颜色即可零冲突满足约束（81 种经典状态中有 3 种能量完全一致），系统从此无需任何量子叠加。但代价立竿见影：最低能层虽含 15 个态，在顶点置换下却完全平庸，退化为单一一列，不再存在“第二列”，物质“三代”随之消失；同时，沿回路循环平移一格的时钟算符亦失去非平庸相位，再也无法衍生出虚数单位 i。一个失去内部几何阻挫的系统无法长出任何复杂结构。因此，“求异”的反铁磁符号绝非个人偏好，而是唯一允许复杂结构涌现的选择。两条完全独立的论证——一条诉诸复时钟能否稳定形成，另一条检验三角形上的三色叠加能否满足规范中性——最终共同收敛于这一唯一构造。框架所需的前提仅有唯一一句公设：此类 K₄ 单元存在并形成晶格；其余所有结构皆为定理。
rows.rides: 不依赖任何开放接口。其成立范围与第 01 项完全一致：处于作者界定的模型范畴内，并接受唯一物理假设——此类元胞真实存在并铺成晶格。
rows.check: 《K4 元胞》一章“元胞自举定理”全部五项条款及其后附注；审阅问题 A。机器核验侧：五个 Lean 模块，零 sorry，所依赖公理不超出 Lean 数学库标准三条逻辑公理；其中图论条款已在全部 64 个带标号四顶点图上完成穷举验证；符号选择条款则通过两条推导路线下的能级不等式完成机器认证（CellBootstrapSignNormalisation）。模块源码内附带的三项诚实标注（不动点具体表述、算术极小性、图类限定）目前仍由作者保留为开放审阅项。此外，定理末尾关于“读出即告闭合”的表述已被勘误 E10 明确收窄限制。
rows.lead: 四个顶点、三种颜色、六条全连接边及“求异”的符号法则，无一源于主观偏好。

whys.h2: One journey: from four points to the universe.
whys.intro: Eleven things that, inside this framework, could not have been otherwise. All of them are read off the same four-point object. They are ordered by how solid the evidence is, not by how surprising they are. Rows 01 and 04 are about the finite object alone; you can check them yourself without taking the framework on trust. In rows 02 and 03 the counting half is closed in the same way, but the half that lands on spacetime runs through interfaces the author lists as open.
whys.scaleNote: The strip marks where each answer lives in nature, not what the framework computes. The length at its left-hand end is the cell’s own unit of length: a scale that is set, not a result that is derived.

rows.q: Why does the object have four corners?
rows.answer: i has one non-negotiable property: it squares to −1, so doing it twice is a U-turn. This cell grows an i of its own: its clock is the loop through the four corners, and one step round that loop is taken to be the unit itself. With n corners a step turns through 360°/n, and two steps must make exactly a U-turn: 2 × 360°/n = 180°, whose only solution is n = 4. Three corners turn 240° in two steps, five turn 144°: no U-turn either way. The cell has four corners because i has order four — do it four times and you are back where you started. Not a slogan, a division. Other clauses of the same theorem fix the number of colours: it must be odd (an even number lets in an element that cannot tell left from right — the author’s own criterion), at least three, and fewer than the corners. Give it a fourth colour, one per corner, and the object has one lonely perfect answer with no generations in it. Odd, at least three, fewer than four: of every (colours, corners) pair, only (3, 4) survives.
rows.rides: Nothing open. It has a scope: the class of objects the author marks out himself — one three-setting elementary switch per point of a graph, pairwise interactions only — plus the framework’s single postulate, that such cells exist in lattices. How wide that class is, he lists as one of his own review targets.
rows.check: The cell-bootstrap theorem, clause (i), K4-cell chapter; review Target A. Machine side: the quarter-turn clock squares to −I and a three-fold clock provably cannot (CellBootstrapFixedPoint). A companion module excludes every n ≥ 5 by a different count: such clocks carry more than one complex pair (CellBootstrapClockUniqueness). Lean certifies those arithmetic clauses, zero sorry; that the clauses are physically necessary is the monograph’s argument, not the machine’s.
rows.lead: The object has four corners because a quarter turn done twice is a U-turn — and turning around is exactly what multiplying by −1 does.

rows.q: Why are there three generations of matter?
rows.answer: The cell has 81 basic states: four corners, three colours at each, 3 × 3 × 3 × 3. Work out its energies — an 81-by-81 matrix, a second on a laptop — and they sort into four floors, 15, 45, 12, 9, with nothing left over. The ground floor holds 9, laid out as a 3 × 3 grid: the three rows are colour, and the three columns come from the corners being interchangeable, since swapping them freely leaves only three independent directions, four minus one. Those three columns are the three generations of matter. When the muon turned up, the physicist I. I. Rabi asked, “Who ordered that?” Nobody did: the ground floor was always three columns wide. The same arithmetic says one column stands alone and two come as a pair — one heavy generation and two light ones. It fixes the shape, not the masses. Counting to three is a theorem; carrying those three columns onto spacetime as three families of quarks and leptons is a set of named interfaces the author himself lists as open.
rows.rides: The count itself: nothing open. Turning that “three” into three generations of particles on spacetime, and matching the anonymous seven rows to the Standard Model’s seven kinds of particle, is a set of four named maps the author lists as open (E8).
rows.check: “Flavour generations from Schur–Weyl duality”, K4-cell chapter, with the remark “Colour vs flavour: no category confusion”; numerical certificate Experiment 071 (exact diagonalisation, degeneracies 9, 12, 45, 15 from the ground floor up). Strictly, the three columns live in the [2,1,1] Specht module of S₄: the standard module [3,1] with one sign twist attached, same dimension three. The one-heavy-two-light shape is the mass-protection lemma. The open side is the four named maps of erratum E8: global generation extension, full normal embedding, real physical-branch preservation, 48-row current-symbol surjectivity. Bounded also by E10; review Targets 8 and 10.
rows.lead: The object’s lowest level is three columns wide. That three is counted, not put in; landing it on real particles is a further step.

rows.q: Why does spacetime have four dimensions?
rows.answer: A smooth globe can be turned in three independent ways. Stick a pin in it: the turn about the pin’s axis leaves it where it is, the other two move it, and every place the pin can go makes up the surface, two-dimensional: 3 − 1 = 2. Now replace the globe with this cell. It too can be turned, in eight independent ways, and the ground state is the pin: exactly four of those turns leave it alone, four move it. Every place the ground state can go is an 8 − 4 = 4-dimensional space; stitch those local nudges together from place to place and that continuous space is spacetime. Time has not entered yet: the four directions look exactly alike. Then the ground state’s own clock (the jargon is modular flow) picks one of the four, wherever that clock runs, and flips the sign of its ruler. That one is time: 3 + 1, not 4 + 1. A second route props the answer up from below. The small asymmetry between matter and antimatter — CP violation in quark mixing — is, in the form this framework gives it, a four-direction quantity, and a universe with fewer dimensions has no room to hold it. The four corners and the four dimensions are two different fours: one whole-number arithmetic, the other a subtraction of continuous symmetries. Two birth certificates, then one axle — and that axle is the framework’s stated identification, not a coincidence.
rows.rides: The step that cuts the eight turns down to the four that leave the ground state alone — SU(3) broken down to U(2) — is internal, and closed. Until that clock supplies time, the four dimensions are Euclidean: all four alike, none of them yet time. The passage from there to a world that has a time direction (Euclidean to Lorentzian), and how gravity itself enters at the start, are interfaces the author lists as open (E7).
rows.check: “Four spacetime dimensions as topological necessity”, K4-cell chapter: the topological-necessity theorem (the 8 − 4 = 4 coset count) and the Berry-form CP obstruction theorem (a (2,2) form vanishes identically below four dimensions), both marked closed in the monograph; the “fourfold selection of D = 4” is a remark, not a theorem. The time step: the modular-flow Wick-rotation lemma and the “modular time is not a fifth dimension” remark, closed on the regular chart; the machine side only returns the supplied signature. Lean: the coset arithmetic has a proved core, the CP² geometry is not formalised, and on the CP obstruction the machine only takes in “Jarlskog ≠ 0 ⇒ at least four dimensions” as a premise and hands it back — not an independent check. Erratum E7; review Targets 2 and 3.
rows.lead: Eight ways to turn the object; four leave its lowest state alone. Four directions are left, and the framework reads those as spacetime.

rows.q: Why was nothing else about the object chosen either?
rows.answer: It is not only the four. Within the class of objects the author marks out, every structural feature of the cell is forced by consistency: four corners, three colours, the complete graph, an interaction that simply swaps the two ends, one strength shared by every link, and the sign that says “differ”. No experimental number enters any clause. The sign you can test on paper. Reverse the rule to “agree”, so every link wants its two ends alike, and the problem vanishes: all four corners wear red, 3 of the 81 states break no link, and no quantum superposition is needed. The price arrives immediately. The bottom floor now has 15 states in a single column — swapping corners changes nothing, so there is no second column and no “generation” — and the clock that turned “rotate one step” into i now turns as if it had not turned at all. A universe that has stopped straining grows nothing. So “differ” is not the author’s taste: it is the one sign under which anything grows, and two independent calculations — one reading the clock, one reading whether three colours on a triangle can make a neutral — stop at the same answer. The framework assumes one sentence and no more: such cells exist, and in lattices. The rest of their structure is a theorem.
rows.rides: Nothing open. Same scope as row 01: the class the author marks out, plus the one postulate — that such cells exist in lattices.
rows.check: The cell-bootstrap theorem, all five clauses, and the remark that follows it, K4-cell chapter; review Target A. Machine side: five Lean modules, zero sorry, no axioms beyond the three standard logical axioms of the mathematics library; the graph clause exhaustively checked on all 64 labelled graphs; for the sign clause, what is certified is the energy-level inequalities along both routes (CellBootstrapSignNormalisation). Three honesty flags inside those modules (fixed-point formulation, arithmetic minimality, graph choice) are still marked open by the author. Erratum E10 narrows the “readout closes it” sentence that ends the theorem.
rows.lead: Four points, three colours, six links, the rule that says “differ”: not one of them was chosen.
